ready2_open_rewrite.final_cot: First describe the image: the gray shading in the figure represents the urban area, and there is point M near the urban area; around M are distributed audible noise contours such as 65, 75, 85, and 95 PNdB; the high-noise-value area is close to M, and extends outward in a belt shape along the operating direction of the transportation vehicles. The figure also marks four black transportation nodes A, B, C, and D, among which A is on the northwest side of the urban area, B is on the west side of the urban area, D is on the south side of the urban area and relatively nearby, and C is in the southwest direction of the urban area and relatively farther away. Then reason: if place M is relocated as a whole, the existing noise contour shape and transportation operation direction should be approximately translated to the candidate points to judge the affected range. A, B, and D are relatively close to the urban area, or the extension direction of the noise belt can easily approach and affect the gray urban area, so after relocation they may still affect urban residents. C is located in the distant southwestern suburbs of the urban area, and the noise belt and the urban area position are relatively staggered; after overall relocation, the noise impact on urban residents is relatively small, so it is relatively reasonable.
